summary: Princeton admits students without regard to their ability to pay, including international students, and meets full need with grants rather than loans. Since 2025–26, most families earning up to $150,000 pay nothing, and most earning up to $250,000 pay no tuition.
covers: Need-blind admission and aid that meets 100% of demonstrated need with grants — no loans.
Most families with incomes up to $150,000: the full cost of attendance covered — tuition, housing, food, books and personal expenses.
Most families with incomes up to $250,000: no tuition.
eligibility: First-year applicants from any country applying to Princeton's undergraduate college.
Aid is calculated from family income and assets; the published thresholds assume typical assets.
how_to_apply: Apply through one of the application platforms Princeton accepts (such as the Common Application or QuestBridge) with Princeton's supplement.
Choose Single-Choice Early Action (1 November) or Regular Decision (1 January).
Submit the CSS Profile and Princeton's aid documents by the stated deadlines.
Ask for an application fee waiver if needed.
watch_out: Princeton's supplement essays carry weight — start them early and check the current writing requirements.
Aid is decided after admission, but missing aid documents can delay your offer.
Use Princeton's aid estimator to check your family's expected contribution before applying.

sources.title: Princeton University — Princeton enhances financial aid again (August 2025)
